_what: The duplication burn-down, keyed to the scanner's own output. Every pair of files jscpd finds duplicating 20+ lines is an item; it leaves this list by being FIXED (the duplication goes, and the row must go with it) or stays with a written reason. The count of pairs in neither state is the burn-down number. See scripts/cloneLedger.mjs for why this replaced a proxy worklist.
_method: Before fixing a pair, break the source it covers two or three times and check the suites catch it. Caught -> the duplication is real, share it. Survives -> the tests are shallow and duplicated BECAUSE they are; fix what they assert first and the duplication usually dissolves. On the first item this inverted the answer. Full reasoning in scripts/cloneLedger.mjs. A pair whose two files are the SAME file, with overlapping ranges, is usually a detector artifact: jscpd matches a token stream, so the arrange-render-assert rhythm of a large suite reads as one long clone while every literal differs. Check for an identical window before believing it.

adjudicated.tests/features/projects-dashboard/ui/com: A file compared against ITSELF, and the two ranges overlap (24-274 against 14-171), which is the signature of self-similarity rather than two copies. Verified: no two identical 20-line windows exist anywhere in the file. jscpd matches a TOKEN stream, so the arrange-render-assert rhythm of 30 tests — const project, renderWithProvider, expect — reads as one 251-line clone while every literal differs. The suite already uses createProjectsDashboardProject and renderWithProvider; there is nothing left to lift.
